neighbours.label: the vehicle of an analogy: the thing something is likened to ('is like X', 'looks like X', 'think of A as X', 'the analogy of X')
fire: Her new novel is like the Abbey Road of crime fiction.
Seen from the valley, the peak looks like a giant wearing a cloak.
Think of the immune system as an army guarding a castle.
The teacher used the analogy of a library to explain memory.
At night the city resembles a field of glowing fireflies.
His argument works like a house of cards ready to fall.
Picture the atom as a tiny solar system with planets.
The debate was like a chess match between grandmasters.
quiet: Her new novel is the third book in a crime series.
Seen from the valley, the peak is covered in fresh snow.
The immune system protects the body from many infections.
The teacher explained how memory works using a short video.
At night the city is quiet except for a few taxis.
His argument rests on data from three large surveys.
The atom has a small nucleus surrounded by electrons.
The debate lasted two hours and covered many topics.
